title: Budget and Revenue
text:
This page looks at how movie budgets relate to box office revenue. Figure 1 shows that movies with bigger budgets tend to make more money.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (Million USD)")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide Revenue (Million USD)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film Budget vs. Worldwide Revenue

title: The Bond Films
text:
This page looks at how James Bond movies performed at the box office over time.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]

The Bond movies in this dataset were released between 1995 and 2021.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide Revenue (Million USD)")
plt.show()

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
This page looks at how movie length relates to IMDb ratings. Figure 1 shows the relationship between the two.
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (Minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb Rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Movie Runtime vs. IMDb Rating
